proof:
Conventions. X is an extended metric space whose measurable structure is its Borel σ-algebra. ediam S ∈ [0, ∞] is the extended diameter `Metric.ediam S` (written `ediam` under `open Metric`); ediam ∅ = 0. μH[d] is Mathlib's unnormalized d-dimensional Hausdorff measure `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d`, evaluated as an outer measure on arbitrary (possibly non-measurable) sets. Arithmetic is in [0, ∞] with 0·∞ = 0; x^a for x ∈ [0, ∞] and real a is `ENNReal.rpow`. For S ⊆ X and a real exponent a put w_a(S) := ⨆_{S ≠ ∅} (ediam S)^a, the supremum over the proposition S ≠ ∅, so w_a(S) = (ediam S)^a if S ≠ ∅ and w_a(∅) = 0 (in particular w_0(∅) = 0 although (ediam ∅)^0 = 1). λ¹ = volume on ℝ. f is L-Lipschitz on A: edist(f x, f y) ≤ L·edist(x, y) for x, y ∈ A. The siblings used are near_optimal_cover (`slicing_im_coarea_eil_near_optimal_cover`), liminf_cover_bound (`slicing_im_coarea_eil_liminf_cover_bound`) and cover_majorant (`slicing_im_coarea_eil_cover_majorant`), each applied with the same space X.

1. (Case L = 0.) For x, y ∈ A, edist(f x, f y) ≤ 0·edist(x, y) = 0, so f(x) = f(y). Hence the image f(A) ⊆ ℝ has at most one point; it is a subsingleton, hence countable (`Set.Subsingleton.countable`), hence Borel (`Set.Countable.measurableSet`) and λ¹-null (`Set.Countable.measure_zero`, Lebesgue measure has no atoms). Let ψ be the indicator of f(A) with constant value ∞. It is measurable. If t ∈ f(A), then ψ(t) = ∞ ≥ μH[m](A ∩ f⁻¹{t}). If t ∉ f(A), then A ∩ f⁻¹{t} = ∅ (a point x ∈ A with f(x) = t would put t in f(A)), so μH[m](A ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 ≤ ψ(t). Finally ∫ψ dλ¹ = ∞·λ¹(f(A)) = ∞·0 = 0 ≤ 2L·μH[m+1](A) (`lintegral_indicator_const`). This settles L = 0; assume L ≠ 0 from now on.

2. (Case μH[m+1](A) = ∞.) Let ψ be the constant function ∞. It is measurable and the pointwise bound is trivial. Since L ≠ 0, 2L ≠ 0, so 2L·∞ = ∞ (`ENNReal.mul_top`) and ∫ψ ≤ ∞ = 2L·μH[m+1](A). Assume μH[m+1](A) ≠ ∞ from now on.

3. (Scales.) For k ∈ ℕ let ρ_k := (k + 1)⁻¹ ∈ [0, ∞] (inverse in [0, ∞] of the cast of k + 1). Then ρ_k > 0 (`ENNReal.inv_pos`, since k + 1 ≠ ∞), and ρ_k → 0 as k → ∞ (`ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero` composed with k ↦ k + 1, `tendsto_add_atTop_nat`).

4. (Covers.) For each k apply near_optimal_cover with d := m + 1 (the real cast of the natural number m + 1; d ≥ 0), the set A, r := ρ_k and ε := ρ_k (both > 0) and μH[m+1](A) ≠ ∞. Choosing for every k (`choose`), we get sets S_{k,i} ⊆ A (k, i ∈ ℕ) with A ⊆ ⋃_i S_{k,i}, ediam S_{k,i} ≤ ρ_k, and Σ_i w_{m+1}(S_{k,i}) ≤ μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k.

5. (Majorants.) For each k apply cover_majorant to m, f, L, A (with the Lipschitz hypothesis) and the family (S_{k,i})_{i ∈ ℕ}, whose members lie in A by step 4. Choosing for every k, we get Borel functions ψ_k : ℝ → [0, ∞] with
 (i) Σ_i w_m(S_{k,i} ∩ (A ∩ f⁻¹{t})) ≤ ψ_k(t) for every t ∈ ℝ, and
 (ii) ∫ψ_k dλ¹ ≤ 2L·Σ_i w_{m+1}(S_{k,i}) ≤ 2L·(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k), the second inequality by step 4 and monotonicity of multiplication by 2L.

6. (The majorant.) Define ψ(t) := liminf_{k→∞} ψ_k(t). It is Borel as the liminf of a sequence of Borel functions (`Measurable.liminf`).

7. (Pointwise bound.) Fix t ∈ ℝ and put B := A ∩ f⁻¹{t}. Apply liminf_cover_bound with d := m (real cast), s := B, the sequence ρ of step 3 (ρ_k → 0) and T_{k,i} := S_{k,i} ∩ B. Its hypotheses hold: ediam T_{k,i} ≤ ediam S_{k,i} ≤ ρ_k (`Metric.ediam_mono`, step 4); and for every k, if x ∈ B then x ∈ A ⊆ ⋃_i S_{k,i}, so x ∈ S_{k,i} ∩ B for some i, i.e. B ⊆ ⋃_i T_{k,i}. Hence μH[m](B) ≤ liminf_k Σ_i w_m(S_{k,i} ∩ B). By 5(i), Σ_i w_m(S_{k,i} ∩ B) ≤ ψ_k(t) for every k, so by monotonicity of liminf (`Filter.liminf_le_liminf`) μH[m](A ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ≤ liminf_k ψ_k(t) = ψ(t).

8. (Integral bound.) By Fatou's lemma for measurable functions (`lintegral_liminf_le`), ∫ψ dλ¹ = ∫ liminf_k ψ_k dλ¹ ≤ liminf_k ∫ψ_k dλ¹, and by 5(ii) and monotonicity of liminf this is ≤ liminf_k 2L·(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k). The sequence μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k converges to μH[m+1](A) + 0 = μH[m+1](A) (constant plus ρ_k → 0, `Filter.Tendsto.add`), and multiplication by the finite constant 2L (2L ≠ ∞ because L is a finite nonnegative real) preserves this limit (`ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul`). A convergent sequence has liminf equal to its limit (`Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq`), so liminf_k 2L·(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k) = 2L·μH[m+1](A). Hence ∫ψ dλ¹ ≤ 2L·μH[m+1](A), and ψ has all required properties. ∎

Remark. The case analysis mirrors step 6 of the parent proof. The two degenerate cases use explicit majorants (the ∞-valued indicator of the at most one-point set f(A) when L = 0, and the constant ∞ when L ≠ 0 and μH[m+1](A) = ∞), so no covers are needed there; this is why the statement holds on an arbitrary extended metric space without separability.
key_steps: L = 0: f is constant on A; ψ := ∞·1_{f(A)} works since f(A) is countable, hence Borel and λ¹-null.
L ≠ 0 and μH[m+1](A) = ∞: ψ :≡ ∞ works since 2L·∞ = ∞.
Otherwise, for ρ_k = (k+1)⁻¹ take near-optimal covers S_{k,·} of A (near_optimal_cover) and their majorants ψ_k (cover_majorant) with ∫ψ_k ≤ 2L(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k).
ψ := liminf_k ψ_k is Borel; liminf_cover_bound applied to T_{k,i} := S_{k,i} ∩ A ∩ f⁻¹{t} gives μH[m](A ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ≤ ψ(t).
Fatou (lintegral_liminf_le) and convergence of 2L(μH[m+1](A) + ρ_k) give ∫ψ ≤ 2L·μH[m+1](A).
